process.title: Implement tapcode.py (5x5 tap code, C/K merged) with tests
process.scope: Owns only the new files tapcode.py and tests/test_tapcode.py. Does not touch any existing file, does not implement bell or decimaltime, does not import from other modules.
process.task:
Implement tapcode.py for Tap code (5×5 grid, C/K merged). Use only the Python standard library. Do not import bell or decimaltime.

The 5×5 table is fixed (rows and columns are 1-based): row 1 = A B C D E; row 2 = F G H I J; row 3 = L M N O P; row 4 = Q R S T U; row 5 = V W X Y Z. The table contains no K: K merges with C — encoding K yields C's coordinate (1, 3), and decoding (1, 3) returns "C".

`tapcode_encode(text: str) -> list[tuple[int, int]]`: preprocess text to uppercase and keep only A–Z (K counts as C); each letter yields its (row, col). Non-str input raises TypeError (e.g. tapcode_encode(42) raises TypeError). Empty string returns [].

`tapcode_decode(pairs) -> str`: pairs must be a list or tuple, each item a (row, col) numeric pair. If pairs itself is not a list/tuple (a str is also rejected) it raises TypeError; malformed pair shapes or non-int coordinates (bool rejected) raise TypeError; coordinates outside 1–5 raise ValueError. An empty list returns "".

Acceptance examples — every one of these must have a corresponding test case in tests/test_tapcode.py (逐字 transcribed from the work order):
- tapcode_encode("A") == [(1, 1)]
- tapcode_encode("C") == [(1, 3)]
- tapcode_encode("K") == [(1, 3)] (merged with C)
- tapcode_encode("HELLO") == [(2, 3), (1, 5), (3, 1), (3, 1), (3, 4)]
- tapcode_encode("Z") == [(5, 5)]
- tapcode_encode("") == []
- tapcode_encode("tap code!") == [(4, 4), (1, 1), (3, 5), (1, 3), (3, 4), (1, 4), (1, 5)] (preprocessing: uppercase, keep only A–Z)
- tapcode_decode([(2, 3), (1, 5), (3, 1), (3, 1), (3, 4)]) == "HELLO"
- tapcode_decode([(1, 3)]) == "C"
- tapcode_decode([]) == ""
- Round trip: tapcode_decode(tapcode_encode("WORLD")) == "WORLD"; tapcode_decode(tapcode_encode("TAPCODE")) == "TAPCODE"
- tapcode_decode([(0, 3)]), tapcode_decode([(3, 6)]), tapcode_decode([(6, 1)]) each raise ValueError
- tapcode_decode([("1", 3)]), tapcode_decode([(1,)]), tapcode_decode("13"), tapcode_encode(42) each raise TypeError

Constraints: only create tapcode.py and tests/test_tapcode.py (both new files); do not modify any existing file; standard library only.

Checks (run from repository root, verbatim from work order): python3 -m pytest tests/test_tapcode.py -q and python3 -m pytest tests/ -q
